content.text:
Start at https://www.google.com and complete the following task.

I'm seriously thinking about boarding school for my child for high school, and I want a solid college-prep shortlist I can actually look through myself afterward. Please start on Google and use credible ranking or review sources to identify about 15 to 20 of the strongest U.S. boarding schools with strong academic reputations, then for each school open the actual admissions page in its own tab so I can compare them side by side. As you go, please make sure each school really does offer boarding and is clearly a college-preparatory high school, not just a day school or a specialty program. Then create a CryptPad Sheets spreadsheet called Top Boarding Schools and log each verified school with the school name, city and state, annual boarding tuition or total boarding cost, application deadline if the admissions site lists one, and the direct admissions page link. I also want browser-proof here, so please leave every admissions tab open for the schools you include, and if a tuition or deadline is buried on a separate tuition or apply page, open that page long enough to verify it before recording the number and then keep the admissions tab available. Once the sheet is filled out with around 15 to 20 strong options, add a short summary in the sheet or a companion CryptPad Document about the typical tuition range and where these schools are concentrated geographically, and finish with a brief recommendation note about the most compelling options so I have a practical starting point.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

or who connect with us during admission events, to be fully present during those valuable experiences. We do not offer in-person interviews, on campus or otherwise.
	 
	All interviews will be weighed equally in the Choate application, regardless of the interviewer. 
	 
	The interview appointment is scheduled for 45 minutes. The interviewer will speak individually (one-on-one) with the prospective student for the first 20-25 minutes of the appointment.


If you have any questions about interviewing or visiting our campus, please visit our FAQ page or email us.


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Submit Standardized Tests
	
	
		
	

				
			Standardized test scores are an optional part of the application to Choate. If you choose to submit test scores with your application, please see below for testing options based on the grade to which you are applying.

9th grade applicants: Submit SSAT or ISEE scores taken on or after June.

10th and 11th grade applicants: Submit SSAT, ISEE, PSAT, SAT or ACT scores taken on or after last June.

Postgraduate applicants: Submit PSAT, SAT or ACT scores taken on or after June from two years ago.

English Proficiency Tests: Non-native English speakers and/or students who have not been at a school where English is the primary language of instruction for at least two years are strongly encouraged to submit results from a TOEFL, Duolingo, or IELTS test taken on or after June.


	


	
	
	

				
			Standardized testing for our admission process depends on the grade to which you are applying.


	
		
			Grades 9, 10
			SSAT, or ISEE
		
		
			Grade 11
			SSAT, ISEE, PSAT, SAT, or ACT
		
		
			Grade PG
			SAT, or ACT
		
		
			Non-Native English Speakers
			TOEFL, IELTS
		
	


 


	


	
	
	

				
			How to send

Official scores should be sent directly from the testing agencies whenever possible. In lieu of sending official score reports for the PSAT, SAT, and ACT tests, a school counselor may submit verified test scores on behalf of the applicant. 

Please use the following codes when registering for a test to have your test results sent directly to Choate:


	
		
			SAT

			TOEFL

If you have questions about our test-optional process please visit our FAQ page. If you seek a fee waiver for standardized tests, please contact us at  admission@choate.edu. 


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Complete the Application
	
	
		
	

				
			Part 1 of the Application

To initiate a Choate application, register with Gateway to Prep Schools, complete the Candidate Profile, and submit it to Choate.

Part 2 of the Application



Complete Part 2 of the Gateway to Prep Schools application for Choate Rosemary Hall. This consists of Applicant Essays and a Parent/Guardian Statement.

Part 3 of the Application

Principal/Counselor Recommendation and Transcript Report

Through Gateway to Prep Schools, request that a school official complete the Principal/Counselor Recommendation as well as the Transcript Report. Your transcript should include your current grades alongside your academic record from the last 2 years. Applicants who are currently in grades 9-12, we ask that your counselor submits the high school profile sheet (if available) with your current grades and transcript(s).

Current English and Mathematics Teacher Recommendations

Request recommendations from your current* English and mathematics teachers through Gateway to Prep Schools. 

*Postgraduate applicants may submit teacher recommendations from either a current or previous year teacher. If you are a 9th-11th grade applicant and are unable to submit recommendations from your current teachers, please contact us at admission@choate.edu.

Third Teacher Recommendation and Personal Recommendation

The Third Teacher Recommendation is optional and may be completed by a current or previous year teacher. 

The Personal Recommendation is optional and may be completed by an adult who knows you well and can speak to your character.

Request either or both of these optional recommendations through Gateway to Prep Schools.

			For students who are applying for financial aid, please complete the Financial Aid Application by January 15.

			Your first step towards admission at Choate Rosemary Hall is to complete the Inquiry Form.

You will be added to our mailing list, and the information you share will help us get to know you and your interests. By submitting the inquiry form, you will also receive more information about admission events.


	


	
	
	

				
				Steps to Apply
	
	
		    
        
            
                Inquire
                
            
            
                Schedule an Interview

				Inquire
	
	
		
	

				
			To learn more about Choate Rosemary Hall and to be added to our mailing list, please complete the Inquiry Form. The information you provide in this form will allow us to get to know you and your interests. Upon completion, you will receive more information about Choate and you will be invited to interview opportunities and admission events.


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Schedule an Interview
	
	
		
	

				
			
	An admission interview is strongly encouraged and must be completed during the current application cycle. We can accommodate only one admission interview per applicant.
	 
	Choate conducts interviews between September and February for those students who intend to apply for the following fall.
	 
	After submitting an Inquiry Form to Choate, students will be invited to sign up for an interview via email. 
	 
	All admission interviews take place online. The online format provides a more equitable experience for our applicants and allows families who visit our campus, or who connect with us during admission events, to be fully present during those valuable experiences. We do not offer in-person interviews, on campus or otherwise.
	 
	All interviews will be weighed equally in the Choate application, regardless of the interviewer. 
	 
	The interview appointment is scheduled for 45 minutes. The interviewer will speak individually (one-on-one) with the prospective student for the first 20-25 minutes of the appointment.


If you have any questions about interviewing or visiting our campus, please visit our FAQ page or email us.


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Submit Standardized Tests
	
	
		
	

				
			Standardized test scores are an optional part of the application to Choate. If you choose to submit test scores with your application, please see below for testing options based on the grade to which you are applying.

9th grade applicants: Submit SSAT or ISEE scores taken on or after June.

10th and 11th grade applicants: Submit SSAT, ISEE, PSAT, SAT or ACT scores taken on or after last June.

Postgraduate applicants: Submit PSAT, SAT or ACT scores taken on or after June from two years ago.

English Proficiency Tests: Non-native English speakers and/or students who have not been at a school where English is the primary language of instruction for at least two years are strongly encouraged to submit results from a TOEFL, Duolingo, or IELTS test taken on or after June.


	


	
	
	

				
			Standardized testing for our admission process depends on the grade to which you are applying.


	
		
			Grades 9, 10
			SSAT, or ISEE
		
		
			Grade 11
			SSAT, ISEE, PSAT, SAT, or ACT
		
		
			Grade PG
			SAT, or ACT
		
		
			Non-Native English Speakers
			TOEFL, IELTS
		
	


 


	


	
	
	

				
			How to send

Official scores should be sent directly from the testing agencies whenever possible. In lieu of sending official score reports for the PSAT, SAT, and ACT tests, a school counselor may submit verified test scores on behalf of the applicant. 

Please use the following codes when registering for a test to have your test results sent directly to Choate:


	
		
			SAT
			SSAT
			ISEE
			TOEFL
		
	
	
		
			1883
			2392
			070245
			1883
		
	


If you have questions about our test-optional process please visit our FAQ page. If you seek a fee waiver for standardized tests, please contact us at  admission@choate.edu. 


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Complete the Application
	
	
		
	

				
			Part 1 of the Application

To initiate a Choate application, register with Gateway to Prep Schools, complete the Candidate Profile, and submit it to Choate.

Part 2 of the Application



Complete Part 2 of the Gateway to Prep Schools application for Choate Rosemary Hall. This consists of Applicant Essays and a Parent/Guardian Statement.

Part 3 of the Application

Principal/Counselor Recommendation and Transcript Report

Through Gateway to Prep Schools, request that a school official complete the Principal/Counselor Recommendation as well as the Transcript Report. Your transcript should include your current grades alongside your academic record from the last 2 years. Applicants who are currently in grades 9-12, we ask that your counselor submits the high school profile sheet (if available) with your current grades and transcript(s).

Current English and Mathematics Teacher Recommendations

Request recommendations from your current* English and mathematics teachers through Gateway to Prep Schools. 

*Postgraduate applicants may submit teacher recommendations from either a current or previous year teacher. If you are a 9th-11th grade applicant and are unable to submit recommendations from your current teachers, please contact us at admission@choate.edu.

Third Teacher Recommendation and Personal Recommendation

The Third Teacher Recommendation is optional and may be completed by a current or previous year teacher. 

The Personal Recommendation is optional and may be completed by an adult who knows you well and can speak to your character.

Request either or both of these optional recommendations through Gateway to Prep Schools.

FINANCE OFFICE
Student Account Bills

All tuition and incidental billing is administered through FACTS Management. FACTS will bring you real-time, on-demand billing information, billing statements, and payments in one convenient location, one combined family bill for multi-student families, and the option to enroll in autopay.

FACTS accepts ACH, credit, and debit cards from US banks for auto pay or one-time payments. FACTS accepts international one-time payments securely through Flywire. Please note that not all FACTS portal features are compatible with all browsers. We recommend the use of Chrome or Edge for the best experience.

Bill Payment

The Academy’s preferred way to receive payments is through your FACTS Management Account. Alternatively, check payments can be mailed to Account Receivable, Trustees of Deerfield Academy, PO Box 87, Deerfield, MA 01342. If you need to send a check by express courier service (FedEx, UPS, DHL, etc.), please send it to Accounts Receivable, Deerfield Academy, 7 Boyden Lane, Deerfield, MA 01342.

All checks must be drawn on a United States Bank and be in US Dollars.

The Finance Office does not accept post-dated checks. Checks will be deposited upon receipt. The Academy is not responsible for any bank fees associated with a check that is deposited into our account. Checks or eChecks that are returned by banks for insufficient funds must be redeemed at the Finance Office before any more checks will be accepted. Any fee charged to The Academy for a returned check will be passed on to the student’s account. After three returned checks or eChecks, the Academy will not accept any more checks from that student for the remainder of the school year.

For wire transfer instructions, please contact the Finance Office at finance@deerfield.edu.

Tuition Payment Plans

We offer a monthly tuition payment plan through FACTS Tuition Management. All plans begin in July. The plan offers the flexibility of choosing your payment due date and setting up automatic payments from the checking or credit card account of your choice. Enrollment in a payment plan includes a per family enrollment fee of $55.00.

 

Your Billing Rights

Federal law requires us to advise you in case of errors or questions on your bill. If you think your bill is wrong, or if you need more information about a transaction on your bill, write to Deerfield Academy, Treasurer’s Office, P.O. Box 87, Deerfield, MA 01342-0087, as soon as possible.  We must hear from you no later than 60 days after we send you the first bill on which the error or problem appeared. You can telephone, but doing so will not preserve your rights. In your letter, give the following information:

Your name and account number
The dollar amount of the error
A description and explanation of the error

You do not have to pay any amount in question while we are investigating, but you are still obligated to pay the parts of your bill that are not in question; we cannot report you as delinquent or take any action to collect the amount in question.

OneCards

Students are issued a OneCard at the beginning of each school year. This card is an ID, a key to dorms, and can be used as a debit card for on campus purchases. More information can be found here.

Because this card functions as a key, it is crucial you report the loss or theft of your card immediately through the OneCard portal on DA Info. Please contact the Finance Office or Security for assistance.

Laundry

All dorms have their own laundry room. All machines feature app start and laundry room monitoring, which allows you to see exactly which machines are open and how long it will be until your laundry is done. You will need a Bluetooth-enabled device to start the machines, and your laundry account balance and spending will be tracked in the Mobile Pay/Laundry Connect app. All wash and dry cycles will be $0.05 each, and the minimum app deposit is $10. These machines will not accept coins or cards. 

There are short videos you can watch about using the system and how to download the app.

.

ATM

For cash needs, there is an ATM in the faculty mailroom in the basement of the Main School Building.

Student Checking Accounts

If you would like to establish a personal checking account at a local bank in Greenfield, please visit the bank branch directly to do so. Many families have used Greenfield Cooperative Bank in the past, with whom the Academy has a good relationship. The main branch location is 63 Federal Street in Greenfield, and phone is 413-772-0293. You are responsible for maintaining the account. The Finance Office will cash personal checks up to $250, with the exception of those drawn on overseas checks, you must set up a local bank account. The Finance Office also maintains a limited amount of space where international students may keep passports, travelers’ checks, and similar items.

## 2. Typical Tuition Range & Geographic Concentration

### Typical Tuition Range
- **Published Base Range:** Boarding tuition across these top institutions spans from **$62,740** to **$87,340** for the 2026–2027 academic year.
- **Median Cluster:** The heavy median concentration sits between **$77,000 and $82,000** (e.g., Loomis Chaffee at $77,340; St. Andrew's at $78,500; Andover at $79,800; Deerfield at $79,940; Milton at $79,900; Peddie at $81,000; Taft at $81,400).
- **Cost-Containment Exception:** **Groton School** represents the most pronounced value outlier among elite prep schools at **$62,740**. Groton made a strategic decision under its GRAIN initiative to deliberately cap tuition growth while substantially expanding financial aid. Phillips Exeter Academy also keeps its tuition lower than peer institutions at **$71,797**.
- **Financial Aid Realities:** Every school in this cohort possesses a substantial endowment and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need with direct grant awards (no loans). Crucially, multiple schools—including Exeter, Groton, St. Paul's, Deerfield, and St. Andrew's—have established policies where families with typical assets making under **$150,000/year pay $0 in tuition**.

### Geographic Concentration
- **New England Dominated (12 of 16 schools):** The historical heartland of American boarding schools remains heavily focused in New England:
  - **Massachusetts (6):** Phillips Academy Andover, Groton School, Deerfield Academy, Middlesex School, Milton Academy, Concord Academy.
  - **Connecticut (4):** The Hotchkiss School, Choate Rosemary Hall, The Loomis Chaffee School, The Taft School.
  - **New Hampshire (2):** Phillips Exeter Academy, St. Paul's School.
- **Mid-Atlantic (3 schools):** Strong college-prep powerhouses located in close proximity to the New York / Philadelphia / Washington, D.C. corridor:
  - **New Jersey (2):** The Lawrenceville School, The Peddie School.
  - **Delaware (1):** St. Andrew's School.
- **West Coast (1 school):**
  - **California (1):** Cate School (Carpinteria / Santa Barbara County), representing the leading Pacific coast alternative to the historic New England boarding traditions.

---

## 3. Practical Recommendations & Starting Points

Depending on your child’s learning style, personality, and social preferences, here are the most compelling categories to help narrow down your search:

1. **The Large Flagship Powerhouses:** ***Phillips Exeter Academy (NH)*** & ***Phillips Academy Andover (MA)***
   - *Best for:* Self-directed, intellectually ambitious, and resilient students.
   - *Why:* With over 1,000 students, collegiate-level research facilities, endowments exceeding $1 billion, need-blind admissions, and hundreds of courses (ranging from organic chemistry to multivariable calculus), these schools operate like mini-universities. Both center classroom instruction around the Harkness method (12-student oval table discussions).

2. **The 100% Boarding Communities:** ***St. Paul's School (NH)*** & ***St. Andrew's School (DE)***
   - *Best for:* Students who thrive in total immersion and deeply communal environments.
   - *Why:* Unlike schools where 30% to 50% of the student body commutes daily, 100% of students and faculty reside on campus at SPS and St. Andrew's. This eliminates any day-versus-boarder social divide, keeps weekend campus life vibrant, and generates lifelong student-faculty mentorship. St. Andrew's also features an exceptionally intentional, unpretentious culture on a scenic 2,200-acre campus.

3. **Intimate Scale with Premier Outcomes:** ***Groton School (MA)***
   - *Best for:* Students who desire close teacher mentorship, high warmth, and elite Ivy League / top-20 university placement.
   - *Why:* With ~380 students and a 4:1 student-teacher ratio, every student is known personally by faculty. It combines the rigorous standards of Andover/Exeter with a tight-knit family atmosphere, all while maintaining the lowest tuition rate among top-tier boarding schools ($62,740).

4. **The Residential House System:** ***The Lawrenceville School (NJ)***
   - *Best for:* Students seeking structured residential leadership and campus camaraderie.
   - *Why:* Located five miles from Princeton University, Lawrenceville utilizes a historic House System inspired by Oxford and Cambridge. Underclassmen live in dedicated houses by grade, creating manageable peer communities before transitioning to Fifth Form houses.

5. **Premier West Coast & Outdoor Living:** ***Cate School (CA)***
   - *Best for:* Students who want elite academic rigor paired with an active, outdoor-focused lifestyle.
   - *Why:* Situated on a mesa overlooking the Pacific Ocean and the Santa Ynez Mountains, Cate combines rigorous college preparation and Harkness discussions with an ethos of Western exploration, outdoor sports (surfing, hiking, climbing), and environmental science.

*Application Timing Reminder:* Nearly all schools in this cohort utilize a uniform deadline of **January 15** (with Andover at **February 1**), with admissions decisions released nationwide on **March 10**.

LEAP

Phillips Academy was founded on the idea that an Andover education should be—must be—open and accessible to “youth of requisite qualifications from every quarter.” True to our constitution, we’re one of the few independent schools in the country to admit students regardless of financial need; the official term for this is “need-blind admission.”

We’re also one of the few independent schools to meet 100 percent of each student’s demonstrated financial need—and we meet that need with grants (essentially scholarships), not loans.

We admit students because of their achievement, talent, character, and promise—and then we make sure they’re fully supported.

Tuition and Payment Plans

At Hotchkiss, we believe every student should have the opportunity to excel. This is why we are committed to providing more than $13.9 million in financial support each year to deserving students to ensure that Hotchkiss remains a diverse and vibrant community. Learn more about Financial Aid or use the Financial Aid Estimator to help you plan.

Cost Estimate

The cost of your Hotchkiss tuition may vary slightly from the numbers below. These figures will guide you toward a realistic expectation for the upcoming school year. Our fee breakdown includes the cost of boarding school and day school tuition. This number also includes your technology fee and health services fee.

In addition, you may view a list of common expenses that arise. This may include textbooks, school supplies, laundry and personal spending. View the breakdown below for an idea of how much a typical student spends each month or school year.

Like every part of your journey to Choate, tuition and the financial aid process are treated with intention, care, and inclusion. If it feels like a great fit, let’s make a plan.

Our Approach
We want the world to be here. 

Our families come from everywhere–different countries, regions, cultures, backgrounds, and life experiences–and that's exactly what makes Choate, Choate.  

We will ensure the tuition and financial aid process is clear and affirming. 

We will be present for every step, all the way through. From your first question to your final decision, we're your partner– here to explain, clarify, and support at each part of the process.  

We encourage you to apply for financial aid. 

Financial assistance is simply part of how our families join the Choate community. We hope you won’t hesitate to apply, and we are here to help get you started. 

We evaluate admissions decisions separately. 

Enrollment decisions and financial aid are decided independently, always. 

We want you to see the full Choate, and we want to get to know your full self, independent of financial circumstances

	All interviews will be weighed equally in the Choate application, regardless of the interviewer. 
	 
	The interview appointment is scheduled for 45 minutes. The interviewer will speak individually (one-on-one) with the prospective student for the first 20-25 minutes of the appointment.


If you have any questions about interviewing or visiting our campus, please visit our FAQ page or email us.


	


	
	


	


	
	
	

				
				Submit Standardized Tests
	
	
		
	

				
			Standardized test scores are an optional part of the application to Choate. If you choose to submit test scores with your application, please see below for testing options based on the grade to which you are applying.

9th grade applicants: Submit SSAT or ISEE scores taken on or after June.

	An admission interview is strongly encouraged and must be completed during the current application cycle. We can accommodate only one admission interview per applicant.
	 
	Choate conducts interviews between September and February for those students who intend to apply for the following fall.
	 
	After submitting an Inquiry Form to Choate, students will be invited to sign up for an interview via email. 
	 
	All admission interviews take place online. The online format provides a more equitable experience for our applicants and allows families who visit our campus, or who connect with us during admission events, to be fully present during those valuable experiences. We do not offer in-person interviews, on campus or otherwise.
	 
	All interviews will be weighed equally in the Choate application, regardless of the interviewer. 
	 
	The interview appointment is scheduled for 45 minutes. The interviewer will speak individually (one-on-one) with the prospective student for the first 20-25 minutes of the appointment.

Our Commitment to You 

A St. Paul’s School education is an investment in the future — one that we want to make accessible to as many qualified students as possible. For the 2026-27 academic year, tuition (inclusive of room and board) is $75,400. 

We encourage families who may need assistance covering some or all of tuition to complete a financial aid application. Our financial aid packages meet full demonstrated need. For the 2025-26 school year, more than 200 students received almost $13 million in aid.  

The application process is easier than you may think, and we will help you through every step. 

Meeting the Need

Families of admitted U.S.-based students with an annual household income up to $150,000 generally qualify for full tuition support. Our packages meet admitted students’ full demonstrated need. That means there will be no gap between what we’ve determined you can afford and what we will award, and you will not have to pay anything back.

FINANCIAL AID
Cost should never be a barrier to a Deerfield education.
“Deerfield’s commitment to affordability and access in the form of need-based financial aid is historic, deep, and central to its educational mission. It is founded on the idea—beautifully articulated over a century ago when Frank L. Boyden asked families to ‘pay what you can’—that the Deerfield Experience should be accessible to all young people of promise regardless of means.”—Head of School Dr. John Austin

For more than 40 percent of prospective families, applying to Deerfield Academy also means applying for financial aid. Our Financial Aid Office works with families throughout the application process and, for those who enroll, throughout their Deerfield Experience. We strive to make the process simple, streamlined, and completely confidential.

Step 1: Inquire and Request our Viewbook

We are so glad that you are interested in Deerfield Academy. To receive a Viewbook and learn more about academic and student life, financial aid, and the many opportunities available at Deerfield, please fill out our inquiry form. 

INQUIRE TODAY

Our online application is provided by Gateway to Prep Schools and can be found online at gatewaytoprepschools.com.  

Part I: Candidate Profile

The Candidate Profile is the first part of the Gateway application. Your Candidate Profile should be submitted well in advance of the January 15 application deadline with the appropriate application fee:

For students living in the United States or Canada, the fee is $60.
For students living outside the United States, the fee is $125.

Applicants will have an opportunity to provide or update their extra-curricular information within their Deerfield Admission Portal Account.

Application Fee Waiver:

Once you have submitted your Application Part I: Candidate Profile through our application provider Gateway to Prep Schools, you will receive a link via email providing you with access to the Deerfield Admission Portal. In your Deerfield Portal, you will have the opportunity to schedule appointments, submit additional application materials and complete required items.

FINANCE OFFICE
Student Account Bills

All tuition and incidental billing is administered through FACTS Management. FACTS will bring you real-time, on-demand billing information, billing statements, and payments in one convenient location, one combined family bill for multi-student families, and the option to enroll in autopay.

FACTS accepts ACH, credit, and debit cards from US banks for auto pay or one-time payments. FACTS accepts international one-time payments securely through Flywire. Please note that not all FACTS portal features are compatible with all browsers. We recommend the use of Chrome or Edge for the best experience.

Bill Payment

The Academy’s preferred way to receive payments is through your FACTS Management Account. Alternatively, check payments can be mailed to Account Receivable, Trustees of Deerfield Academy, PO Box 87, Deerfield, MA 01342. If you need to send a check by express courier service (FedEx, UPS, DHL, etc.), please send it to Accounts Receivable, Deerfield Academy, 7 Boyden Lane, Deerfield, MA 01342.

All checks must be drawn on a United States Bank and be in US Dollars.

The Finance Office does not accept post-dated checks. Checks will be deposited upon receipt. The Academy is not responsible for any bank fees associated with a check that is deposited into our account. Checks or eChecks that are returned by banks for insufficient funds must be redeemed at the Finance Office before any more checks will be accepted. Any fee charged to The Academy for a returned check will be passed on to the student’s account. After three returned checks or eChecks, the Academy will not accept any more checks from that student for the remainder of the school year.

For wire transfer instructions, please contact the Finance Office at finance@deerfield.edu.

Tuition Payment Plans

We offer a monthly tuition payment plan through FACTS Tuition Management. All plans begin in July. The plan offers the flexibility of choosing your payment due date and setting up automatic payments from the checking or credit card account of your choice. Enrollment in a payment plan includes a per family enrollment fee of $55.00.

 

Your Billing Rights

Federal law requires us to advise you in case of errors or questions on your bill. If you think your bill is wrong, or if you need more information about a transaction on your bill, write to Deerfield Academy, Treasurer’s Office, P.O. Box 87, Deerfield, MA 01342-0087, as soon as possible.  We must hear from you no later than 60 days after we send you the first bill on which the error or problem appeared. You can telephone, but doing so will not preserve your rights. In your letter, give the following information:

Your name and account number
The dollar amount of the error
A description and explanation of the error

You do not have to pay any amount in question while we are investigating, but you are still obligated to pay the parts of your bill that are not in question; we cannot report you as delinquent or take any action to collect the amount in question.

OneCards

Students are issued a OneCard at the beginning of each school year. This card is an ID, a key to dorms, and can be used as a debit card for on campus purchases. More information can be found here.

Because this card functions as a key, it is crucial you report the loss or theft of your card immediately through the OneCard portal on DA Info. Please contact the Finance Office or Security for assistance.

Laundry

All dorms have their own laundry room. All machines feature app start and laundry room monitoring, which allows you to see exactly which machines are open and how long it will be until your laundry is done. You will need a Bluetooth-enabled device to start the machines, and your laundry account balance and spending will be tracked in the Mobile Pay/Laundry Connect app. All wash and dry cycles will be $0.05 each, and the minimum app deposit is $10. These machines will not accept coins or cards. 

There are short videos you can watch about using the system and how to download the app.

.

ATM

For cash needs, there is an ATM in the faculty mailroom in the basement of the Main School Building.

Student Checking Accounts

If you would like to establish a personal checking account at a local bank in Greenfield, please visit the bank branch directly to do so. Many families have used Greenfield Cooperative Bank in the past, with whom the Academy has a good relationship. The main branch location is 63 Federal Street in Greenfield, and phone is 413-772-0293. You are responsible for maintaining the account. The Finance Office will cash personal checks up to $250, with the exception of those drawn on overseas checks, you must set up a local bank account. The Finance Office also maintains a limited amount of space where international students may keep passports, travelers’ checks, and similar items.

Tuition & Financial Aid

St. Andrew’s is affordable to all students who are qualified for admission, regardless of how much they can pay.

In 1929, our founder envisioned a different kind of boarding school—a school with the highest aspirations and standards, open to the hardest-working, most promising students, regardless of their family's ability to pay. We meet 100% of a family's demonstrated financial need for all admitted students. Our financial aid program and commitment to socioeconomic diversity is the core of who we are: socioeconomic diversity drives our mission, our community, and our culture of inclusion, joy, and authentic human connection. We believe in something bigger than ourselves.

NEW: All families with a combined household income under $150,000 may attend St. Andrew's free of cost.

How to Apply

 

Each year, applications for the following fall are due by January 15. Admissions decisions are sent on March 10. After January 15, we accept applications to our wait list, which we review as space becomes available. 

We are excited to get to know you through the application process. Our favorite essays tell a real, human story. We believe in progress, not perfection—don't strive to write the perfect essay, just write your essay.

Our goal is to ensure that your application process is as frictionless and affirming as possible. Please reach out to the Admissions Office with any questions at 302-285-4231.

Peddie tuition snippet: Tuition & Affordability
TUITION AND AFFORDABILITY

At Peddie, we want extraordinary students to have extraordinary opportunities. Our commitment to access and affordability ensures that our community is full of great students from every economic background. A Peddie education is an investment in a student’s future. Consider us your partners in this investment, every step of the way, starting with the admission process.

Just as our students receive one-on-one encouragement and guidance from our faculty, Peddie’s admission team will help you navigate your next steps toward financial assistance. You will receive individualized guidance from dedicated admission officers during the entire process. If you believe that you may need financial assistance to afford Peddie, we encourage you to apply. You may not know where to begin. You may just have a few questions. Either way, we’re here to support you.

With an endowment in the top ten among all boarding schools in America, the donations from thousands of generous alumni and friends help students across a variety of income levels to afford Peddie.

This year, we allocated $12 million in financial assistance to families. Among students receiving financial assistance, grants cover an average of 70% of their tuition; these grants are on average $57,00

Top U.S. Boarding Schools: Executive Summary & Recommendations

# Top U.S. College-Preparatory Boarding Schools Shortlist

To give you a rigorous, practical starting point for your child’s high school search, 16 of the nation’s strongest college-preparatory boarding schools were identified from credible rankings (including Niche’s 2026 Best Boarding High Schools in America, Boarding School Review, and the Ten Schools Association). 

Each institution was individually verified on its live admissions site to ensure it is a dedicated, college-preparatory high school (grades 9–12) offering a residential boarding program. The annual boarding tuition, application deadline, and direct admissions link were collected from each live site, and the actual admissions portal for each school has been left open in its own browser tab for side-by-side comparison.

---

## 1. Master Shortlist Table

The verified data has been logged in the **CryptPad Sheets** spreadsheet titled **`Top Boarding Schools`**:
- **CryptPad Sheet Link:** https://cryptpad.fr/sheet/#/2/sheet/edit/MtCyjfLbhToDXi8O3SwYrHQ3/
- **Companion CryptPad Document Link:** https://cryptpad.fr/pad/#/2/pad/edit/rV3j-T+m2WSLN8OR3pIm2cuJ/

| 2 | **Phillips Academy Andover** | Andover, MA | $79,800 | February 1 | https://www.andover.edu/admission | Tab 787784274 |

## 2. Typical Tuition Range & Geographic Concentration

### Typical Tuition Range
- **Published Base Range:** Boarding tuition across these top institutions spans from **$62,740** to **$87,340** for the 2026–2027 academic year.
- **Median Cluster:** The heavy median concentration sits between **$77,000 and $82,000** (e.g., Loomis Chaffee at $77,340; St. Andrew's at $78,500; Andover at $79,800; Deerfield at $79,940; Milton at $79,900; Peddie at $81,000; Taft at $81,400).
- **Cost-Containment Exception:** **Groton School** represents the most pronounced value outlier among elite prep schools at **$62,740**. Groton made a strategic decision under its GRAIN initiative to deliberately cap tuition growth while substantially expanding financial aid. Phillips Exeter Academy also keeps its tuition lower than peer institutions at **$71,797**.
- **Financial Aid Realities:** Every school in this cohort possesses a substantial endowment and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need with direct grant awards (no loans). Crucially, multiple schools—including Exeter, Groton, St. Paul's, Deerfield, and St. Andrew's—have established policies where families with typical assets making under **$150,000/year pay $0 in tuition**.

### Geographic Concentration
- **New England Dominated (12 of 16 schools):** The historical heartland of American boarding schools remains heavily focused in New England:
  - **Massachusetts (6):** Phillips Academy Andover, Groton School, Deerfield Academy, Middlesex School, Milton Academy, Concord Academy.
  - **Connecticut (4):** The Hotchkiss School, Choate Rosemary Hall, The Loomis Chaffee School, The Taft School.
  - **New Hampshire (2):** Phillips Exeter Academy, St. Paul's School.
- **Mid-Atlantic (3 schools):** Strong college-prep powerhouses located in close proximity to the New York / Philadelphia / Washington, D.C. corridor:
  - **New Jersey (2):** The Lawrenceville School, The Peddie School.
  - **Delaware (1):** St. Andrew's School.
- **West Coast (1 school):**
  - **California (1):** Cate School (Carpinteria / Santa Barbara County), representing the leading Pacific coast alternative to the historic New England boarding traditions.

## 3. Practical Recommendations & Starting Points

Depending on your child’s learning style, personality, and social preferences, here are the most compelling categories to help narrow down your search:

1. **The Large Flagship Powerhouses:** ***Phillips Exeter Academy (NH)*** & ***Phillips Academy Andover (MA)***
   - *Best for:* Self-directed, intellectually ambitious, and resilient students.
   - *Why:* With over 1,000 students, collegiate-level research facilities, endowments exceeding $1 billion, need-blind admissions, and hundreds of courses (ranging from organic chemistry to multivariable calculus), these schools operate like mini-universities. Both center classroom instruction around the Harkness method (12-student oval table discussions).

2. **The 100% Boarding Communities:** ***St. Paul's School (NH)*** & ***St. Andrew's School (DE)***
   - *Best for:* Students who thrive in total immersion and deeply communal environments.
   - *Why:* Unlike schools where 30% to 50% of the student body commutes daily, 100% of students and faculty reside on campus at SPS and St. Andrew's. This eliminates any day-versus-boarder social divide, keeps weekend campus life vibrant, and generates lifelong student-faculty mentorship. St. Andrew's also features an exceptionally intentional, unpretentious culture on a scenic 2,200-acre campus.

3. **Intimate Scale with Premier Outcomes:** ***Groton School (MA)***
   - *Best for:* Students who desire close teacher mentorship, high warmth, and elite Ivy League / top-20 university placement.
   - *Why:* With ~380 students and a 4:1 student-teacher ratio, every student is known personally by faculty. It combines the rigorous standards of Andover/Exeter with a tight-knit family atmosphere, all while maintaining the lowest tuition rate among top-tier boarding schools ($62,740).

4. **The Residential House System:** ***The Lawrenceville School (NJ)***
   - *Best for:* Students seeking structured residential leadership and campus camaraderie.
   - *Why:* Located five miles from Princeton University, Lawrenceville utilizes a historic House System inspired by Oxford and Cambridge. Underclassmen live in dedicated houses by grade, creating manageable peer communities before transitioning to Fifth Form houses.

5. **Premier West Coast & Outdoor Living:** ***Cate School (CA)***
   - *Best for:* Students who want elite academic rigor paired with an active, outdoor-focused lifestyle.
   - *Why:* Situated on a mesa overlooking the Pacific Ocean and the Santa Ynez Mountains, Cate combines rigorous college preparation and Harkness discussions with an ethos of Western exploration, outdoor sports (surfing, hiking, climbing), and environmental science.

*Application Timing Reminder:* Nearly all schools in this cohort utilize a uniform deadline of **January 15** (with Andover at **February 1**), with admissions decisions released nationwide on **March 10**.
